title: Microsoft Purview: DLP and collection policies for Intune-protected mobile apps
summary: Hold: collection policy automation is incorrectly reported as undocumented. Microsoft documents New-FeatureConfiguration for creating collection policies in Security & Compliance PowerShell, currently in public preview. The roadmap facts and the narrowly stated gaps about the planned mobile integration are supported.

claims.claim: The Intune path reaches the clipboard setting through Apps > Protection > Create policy > iOS/iPadOS > Basics > Apps > Data protection.
claims.quote: Select Apps > Protection. ... Select Create policy and select either iOS/iPadOS or Android. ... On the Basics page ... Apps page ... Data protection page ... including cut, copy, paste, and save-as restrictions.
claims.fix: Add the section heading documented by the already cited iOS settings reference: 'Apps > Protection > Create policy > iOS/iPadOS > Basics > Apps > Data protection > Data Transfer > Restrict cut, copy and paste between other apps'. The final setting is at https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/app-management/protection/ref-settings-ios; the pre-check's missing-label lead does not make this route wrong.

claims.claim: Collection policies determine which events are ingested into Purview.
claims.quote: They let you filter which events from both untrusted and trusted sources are ingested into Purview.

claims.claim: Collection policies are for discovery and collection rather than enforcement and do not themselves block actions.
claims.quote: Collection Policies are designed to streamline discovery of relevant information rather than to apply enforcement on that information.

claims.claim: Solutions > Data Loss Prevention > Classifiers > Collection policies opens the policy list, with + Create policy and + Add activities used to configure collection.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, select Solutions > Data Loss Prevention > Classifiers > Collection policies.
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path to 'Solutions > Data Loss Prevention > Classifiers > Collection policies > + Create policy > + Add activities'. Replace the note's last sentence with 'Select + Create policy, supply a name and any optional conditions, then select + Add activities.' These steps remain documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/collection-policies-create-deploy-policy.

claims.claim: Automation for configuring which events collection policies collect is not documented.
claims.quote: Use the New-FeatureConfiguration cmdlet to create Microsoft Purview feature configurations within your organization, including: Collection policies. ... Includes UploadText and DownloadText activity for all supported classifiers.
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].api null with kind 'powershell', call 'New-FeatureConfiguration -Name <policy-name> -FeatureScenario KnowYourData -Mode Enable -ScenarioConfig <collection-policy-JSON>', and docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/new-featureconfiguration'. Add to the note: 'Security & Compliance PowerShell; public preview, not available in all organizations and subject to change. ScenarioConfig sets Activities, EnforcementPlanes and SensitiveTypeIds; Locations scopes the policy. The reference supplies the JSON syntax and examples.' Update the rendered automation cell to match. This is automation for existing collection policies, not confirmation of mobile integration support.
